DISAGREE. I can settle this from the pinned bytes and the sealed Q alone, without the issue body. Q writes the token with a leading dash ('-delete'), and Section 6's universal pass/fail requires preserving every explicit constraint in Q, so the readings in which '-delete' is a flag/option token are the admissible ones; the annotator's third reading (a 'delete' subcommand answered by AddCommand) is only reachable by discarding a character that Q states. Every admissible reading converges on the same verdict, and on the same deciding fact: cobra declares no flag types and no flag-declaration API. Since verdict and disqualifier are both determinable, the row is not genuinely unsettled and should not block Phase 2. Recommended terminal state: not_answerable, D3 (D5 would also be defensible on the same facts; nothing turns on how hard anything was to find).
